title: Squared paper for Sankey diagrams
subject: Science (GCSE Biology, Chemistry, Physics)
source: Written for gcse-science/y10 lesson 120 (Squared paper for Sankey diagrams (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 120: Efficiency and Sankey diagrams. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

blocks.text: Choose a scale, for example 1 small square = 10 J. Draw the input arrow, then split it into useful and wasted arrows whose widths add up to the input.

model.title: A motor takes in 200 J and does 50 J of useful work.

keywords.def: useful energy output ÷ total energy output × 100%
arrow diagram whose widths show energy amounts
energy transferred to the store we want
energy transferred to stores we do not want
reducing friction with oil or grease

questions.q: An LED gets 20 J and gives 16 J of light. Efficiency as a decimal and a percentage?
Give one way to make a bicycle more efficient.
Core: Draw Sankey diagrams to scale for three devices and answer the 4SD0-style questions (12 marks).
Extend: A 60% efficient motor must deliver 300 J of useful work. Total input?
Stretch: Evaluate replacing ten 60 W filament bulbs with 8 W LEDs. (3)
questions.a: Same light, less input; less heat wasted; lower bills; upfront cost repaid

questions.q: A device has 400 J input and 300 J wasted. Efficiency?
Efficiency of 30 J useful from 120 J total?
Big question: where does 95% of a filament bulb's energy go?
